items.title: For the test months the platform reproduces NAV's result per advisor and commission type inside the tolerance of section 5, or the difference has a class other than engine (A1-D-004). Where NAV and the approved rule set differ, the approved rule set applies
The comparison report lists each difference with a reason code and a note. A repeated run gives the same result
A past period, recalculated after a change to the structure or a point value, gives the result of the structure in force at the time
A settled statement cannot change. A correction appears as a new line in the next open statement with the original order and rate
A second person releases a settings change. The log shows user, date, old value and new value
The monthly run for twice today's statements is not slower than NAV's current run (section 5)

During the parallel run, no platform result goes to the ERP for booking. After the switch, the released result reaches the ERP once per advisor and month, and the ERP returns the credit-note reference
Until the switch the portal shows NAV's statement as binding, and no forecast without a label
Monthly settlement periods with a payment cutoff (a sale counts when paid by a set day) and a statement deadline, as settings

Points per order line from the product point value in the ERP. Reversals that refer to the original order and period, within an adjustable window (today two years). Manual point corrections from the ERP
Point bases: own sales, group sales and activity turnover, including the sales of advisors recruited in the month
Level table with thresholds and rates, a training condition per level, level protection over a rolling window, and a block period
Support commission as a differential, with a minimum activity turnover, a roll-up to the sponsor, and a start-phase minimum rate whose top-up does not affect the upline
Group formation (breakaway) with a time-limited transition rank, once per advisor
Leader commission down to an adjustable depth (today level 4), with leader levels qualified by the own group and the number of first-line groups, and a minimum share of customer sales

Building bonus: the rates of empty deeper levels, paid on level 1; qualification per team over a rolling window (today three months) with counts and weights; automatic qualification after a career jump
Partner status: a discount on own orders, special rates for the partner and the sponsor, exclusion from group points and promotions
Tip-giver commission: an adjustable rate on the first order and a lower adjustable rate on following orders
Bonus programmes that count events in a period and pay an amount or a rate surcharge, with a membership condition and a limit per person
Advisor structure and customer assignments with their history, as a dated copy from the ERP, so that a past period is recalculated against the structure as it was
The settings screen of A1-D-013
The voucher cost rule of A1-D-014, with the two voucher marks read from the ERP (mandatory for all advisors; who pays)
Draft run with an exception list (large corrections, large differences to the previous month, negative statements), release by two persons, an audit trail
Statement per advisor in the portal, down to the customer, the order and the commission type. The released net amount per advisor and month goes to the ERP
A monthly run for twice today's statements is not slower than NAV's current run (section 5)

Comparison with NAV: import of NAV's monthly result per advisor and commission type; comparison per advisor, per type and in total, with a reason code and a note per difference; a monthly report against the switch criteria
Parallel mode: the run produces the statement but no ERP record
Switch: a dated setting, released by two persons of Finance. From that period the run creates the record for the ERP (NAV or Business Central), and NAV's results are no longer imported
Rates that depend on the order type: first order of a customer, repeat order, subscription order
Several plans at the same time, assigned per advisor group, so that existing advisors can stay on the current plan
Rule-set versions and plan comparison: calculate a draft rule set on past months and compare it with the actual result, per advisor and in total, before release
Bonuses for events from the platform's tasks and journeys
Fees per advisor, deducted from the commission as a statement line. A fee that Provital charges separately is an ERP invoice

Re-validation before the R2 go-live: the engine calculates one month from Business Central inputs and compares it with the NAV-fed run, with mapped advisor numbers. 57Blocks and TSO-DATA plan and scope this work separately, with R2
The engine calculates the commission types of the approved rule set: the types of handbook 7/2025 and the types whose rule Provital confirms (A1-P-005). A further type follows through change control

The platform calculates the commission and produces the statement. The ERP books the released result on the advisor's creditor account and creates the payment file. The portal explains the amount; an e-mail notification stays
The ERP holds the VAT entitlement per advisor and adds the VAT at payout

57Blocks tests the engine on NAV's history during the build. From R1 it calculates every month next to NAV without booking (the parallel run). NAV calculates and pays until Provital decides the switch

Business Central never calculates commission. The switch happens at the latest at R2; the switch criteria (section 5) are its condition. The parallel run continues until Provital accepts the result. Finance classifies each difference as engine, NAV, data or plan. 57Blocks corrects every difference …
R1 starts with the plan in force. Plan changes follow the switch. If Provital changes the plan before the switch, Provital's NAV developer builds the change in NAV as well
Until the switch the portal shows NAV's settled statement as binding. The platform calculates a current-month forecast. Provital sales decides whether advisors see it
In pilot mode NAV calculates the commission for pilot advisors' orders (A7)
An entry package counts for points and commission like a normal purchase. Provital can set a package to zero points later
The catch-all advisor of head office receives a statement that is calculated and not paid
A settled and paid statement never changes. A return, a complaint or a correction enters the next open statement as a new line, valued with the points and the rate of the original order
A return normally comes within two months, a complaint within two years. The engine reverses an order up to two years back

The customer protection runs from the customer's last invoice. The protection period is today six months. Each invoice renews it; a changed period applies from the next order. The period is a setting. An order through another advisor's link while the protection runs counts for the protecting …

Every parameter of the plan in force is adjustable from R1, with an effective date. Very few named roles may change one. A second person releases a change; a log records user, date and reason. The management of several plans is R1.x (section 4.3)

Voucher cost rule: an advisor's own voucher reduces the advisor's commission. The company pays a central campaign, and an advisor cannot opt out. The commission uses the net price after the rebate. At R1 no advisor voucher exists (A3-O-003). The rule applies when Provital allows one
Head office enters manual point corrections in the ERP: a plus or minus entry per advisor with a comment, restricted to few people, also as a bulk upload. The engine reads them
The engine recalculates two years back from the migrated structure history and commission inputs. Finance and IT confirm that the data is complete enough
Points per invoice line are taken as booked in the ERP. For a bundle line, the bundle rule (section 5) derives them
Training progress for the level condition comes from the ERP
A later plan uses the capabilities of section 4.3. Provital and 57Blocks plan them at least three months before the plan change
NAV delivers its monthly result per advisor and commission type, and the code of the NAV commission job
Provital's NAV developer builds the NAV import of the platform's released result, with the credit note

NAV's monthly check sheet also shows Sammelbesteller, Fixprovision, Variable Provision and Lieferdirekt, which the handbook does not define. For each type, Provital confirms its rule from the NAV commission job, or confirms that it is no longer paid
Today's tip-giver rates (assumed 10 % and 5 %) and the number of tip-givers per customer
NAV holds the point corrections of A1-D-015, with the comment and the bulk upload. Business Central does the same at R2
An order reaches the ERP once, with the values, advisor and payment reference that the shop used, also after a retry or an ERP outage
The platform sends each order and each new customer once, with a business key. The daily reconciliation lists every difference. The ERP's matching creates or links the contact
The simulated subscription run on migrated data produces every due delivery exactly once, including the cutover night

A delivery whose payment method fails the check at the cutoff is held before the hand-off, with the reason visible to customer and advisor. A charge that fails at shipment shows as an open item in the ERP
A guest order creates a contact in the ERP; the account link follows the legal decision
The checkout offers the methods that the ERP allows for the customer, or card and PayPal without ERP data. The platform never changes a limit, a block or a method
Cart and checkout for a one-off order, a subscription order and an advisor-prepared order, which the customer approves

Checks before the hand-off: address and postal code, stock, duplicate order and customer (the ERP's matching stays the authority), voucher (A2-C-028) and campaign validity. A failed order goes to the clarification queue
Each order carries the price, campaign and voucher used, with their version, the payment reference and status, the attributed advisor and the order type
Repeatable hand-off: an outbox until the ERP confirms, retry after a failure, a number range that cannot collide with the current shop's, a daily reconciliation against the ERP status
During an ERP outage orders wait in the outbox (T2)
Read-only order status from the ERP (accepted, invoiced, shipped with tracking, returned)
Change or cancel an order inside an adjustable window, until the hand-off
Guest checkout: the order is marked so that the ERP creates the contact; the link of guest orders to an account

Return or complaint request from the account and the advisor portal: reason, order, photos. Approval cases follow the self-service rule set (A4). It creates a ticket and an ERP return; the status returns to the account. Inside the withdrawal period it shows the return conditions from A2-P-004
Create a subscription from the checkout or an order: products, quantities, interval, start date, an ERP delivery address of the customer, the payment method

Self-service until the cutoff: products, quantities, pause, skip, move the next delivery, interval, address, payment method, cancel. The shop shows which delivery a change applies to. An address change reaches the ERP before the next hand-off
Schedule settings as listed in the subscription-deadlines rule set (section 5)
Reminder before the cutoff and confirmation after a change (A4)

Due-delivery run: at the cutoff the platform creates the order of each due delivery with the subscription marker and hands it over (A2-C-004). A rule can combine a customer's deliveries due on the same day

Hold rules: a delivery that cannot run is held with a reason; customer and advisor are informed; a retry or skip follows by rule; head office sees it in the subscription cases of the head office portal
The advisor proposes a subscription change; the customer approves it
Customer-service view: search, change, hold and cancel a subscription as the last instance, with an audit trail
Subscription migration from NAV with the next delivery date, products and payment reference; a simulated run shows no lost or duplicated delivery (T1)
Checkout payments by card and iDEAL through the payment provider, and by PayPal through Provital's account. Reference and status go to the ERP with the order
Payment methods per country, customer role and order type as a rule set, inside the methods that the ERP allows (A2-C-022)

Payment agreements for subscriptions: the platform stores the card token and the PayPal billing agreement (existing PayPal agreements reused with Provital's current business account: A2-P-001). Direct-debit data goes to the ERP (mandate: T1-O-007)
The allowed payment methods per customer, read from the ERP, and the default without ERP data (A2-D-007)

The subscription charge. At the cutoff the platform checks the payment method. A delivery with an unusable payment method is held before the hand-off. At the shipment report the platform charges the reported amount and sends the reference to the ERP. A charge that fails after shipment becomes an …

Refunds of card and PayPal payments on request of the ERP, with the requesting user and the reason in the audit trail. A paid order that the ERP cannot fill goes to the clarification queue; head office informs the customer, and the ERP requests the refund
Provider status events (paid, failed, refunded, chargeback) are recorded and forwarded to the ERP
Online withdrawal: the customer declares a withdrawal in the account or through a form without login; the platform confirms receipt and hands it to the ERP (T2-C-006). Texts: A2-P-004

The checkout applies the shipping-fee rules that head office defines in the ERP (DP1 §3.1), for example carrier choice by parcel weight, a free-shipping threshold, customer pickup, loyalty points against the fee. The ERP keeps the points balance; the platform reads it

Vouchers: an article with a negative price, which the ERP manages like an article; the platform shows it and redeems it at the checkout. The checkout supports these condition types: validity period, minimum order value, product or category scope, customer group or role, single use per customer, one …

The customer keeps the subscription self-service until the cutoff (a setting; today seven days before the delivery; Provital may set five). Then the order goes to the ERP and cannot change. The shop says that a later change applies to the next delivery
Subscriptions run in the platform at R1 and after R2. The ERP receives each due delivery as an order with a subscription marker and does not use its own subscription module
A subscription supports card, PayPal, direct debit and payment on invoice (inside the credit limit). iDEAL and prepayment are for one-off orders only. Provital promotes card
Before the hand-off the shop validates address and postal code and checks stock and duplicates
The ERP is the master of an order from the ERP's acceptance. Until then the platform owns the cart, the checkout and the subscription orders; after it, a read-only status copy
The guest checkout stays. Guest orders of one person are linked to the customer account in the background when the law allows it. A guest order creates a contact in the ERP

The ERP holds the blacklist flag, the temporary block and the credit limit. It sends the allowed payment methods per customer; if the ERP data is missing or older than the maximum age (section 5), card and PayPal apply. The platform never changes the blacklist flag, the temporary block, the credit …
From RC, pilot advisors and their customers place one-off orders in the platform. They go to production NAV through the normal hand-off. Subscriptions stay in the current shop until the cutover (A7)

Subscription charging. In R1 the platform charges card and PayPal for a subscription delivery when the ERP reports the shipment (the invoice date). The ERP decides and books a refund; the platform executes it. Direct debit and payment on invoice stay in the ERP. Before R2, Provital and TSO-DATA can …
No payment on invoice for a new customer. An ERP rule can allow it later, for example after five paid orders. The ERP can extend the methods per customer, for example direct debit
The guest checkout asks only for the data that the order needs. The background link starts when legal counsel allows it
For an accepted return, the platform requests the label from the carrier's return service on Provital's account
Access to Provital's PayPal business account, and the export of the billing agreement IDs and their charge history. Reuse works with the current account (checked)
The payment matrix and provider access. 57Blocks proposes the matrix from the current system
NAV exports the active subscriptions with the next delivery date and the payment reference (T1-P-002)
Legal counsel confirms the online withdrawal texts and the return conditions that the return request (A2-C-009) shows inside the withdrawal period

Each of the four entry flows reaches the purchase in at most three checkout steps (address, payment, confirmation), counted from the cart or the prepared basket, with the attribution of the entry in the order

An order that starts on an advisor's link or path carries that advisor as the entry. The ERP applies the protection rule and returns the attributed advisor, and the account shows that advisor. A link does not move a customer who is protected for another advisor. While the fallback of DP1 section 6 …
Each old domain that Provital owns, and each old page of the redirect list, answers with a permanent redirect to the target page
A calculator adds a product to the cart
A voucher from the ERP is redeemed from the read copy under the condition types of A2-C-028, only one per checkout, and the order carries the voucher version
The advisor page is public only inside the structure, the visibility per item and the moderation rule
The figures of the month match the commission run for the same period, and each KPI names its source
Head office creates and changes each page type of A3-C-023 without a developer
A returning customer sees the "what's new" section on the first screen. Analytics events go to the tool only after consent

The main domain with a path per advisor; permanent redirects from the old advisor domains that Provital owns, from the pages of the redirect list, the current shop and the pilot address; the sitemap. The advisor path carries the advisor into the order
A catalogue from the read copy: categories, product pages, search, filters, cross-selling, stock display, points per product, the price for the customer's role and country
The four entry flows: direct visit, advisor link, prepared basket, live sale on a tablet. Each starts the checkout at the right step and carries its attribution
The checkout in at most three steps: address, payment, confirmation, with the payment method by rule, the shipping-fee rules (A2-C-027) and the guest option from R1
Vouchers at the checkout (A2-C-028): redeem from the read copy, one per checkout, with the two marks and the benefit voucher per role. The order carries the voucher and its version
The five calculators; each adds a product to the cart
Re-order from the order history and the back-in-stock reminder
Products of other brands in the ANIfit shop: a normal product page in the ANIfit design with the product images, and the imprint on provital.com
The account: registration, login, a new password at the first login after the migration, the profile, the addresses, the pets, the consents and the preferences
The order view with status and tracking from the ERP copy, the invoice and the delivery note as a document
The subscription view with the changes of A2-C-011
The return or complaint request, with the status of the ticket, within the self-service rules of A4
The vouchers in the profile: the loyalty vouchers for a limited time, and the campaign vouchers reached from the link in the e-mail
Consent and preference management, with a record per consent and its date and source
The advisor page of section 3, with the visibility per item, the AI help and checks, and the moderation
items.release: RC; AI help and checks: R1

items.title: The customer view in the portal: the advisor's own customers, the last orders, the subscriptions (from R1), the pets, the next due contact, and the e-mail to the customer (A4-C-017)
The to-do list with the reason per item, the step lists and the escalation, and the leads with their next step
The prepared basket and the live sale: the advisor builds an order, the customer approves it in their account or on the tablet
The figures of the month for the advisor: points, the level and the progress, the team, the open items and the statement link
The team view for a leader and the field report for head office, from platform data and the ERP data that the interfaces carry
The contact form to head office and the messages, and the event and training entry (A4-C-016)
The KPI definitions as a rule set, each KPI computed from platform data or from a named ERP interface

Page types for content maintenance: the general landing page, the product-focused page, category pages, product pages, content pages with text, image and video blocks, and a page with frequent questions. Head office maintains their content in the content function (A5-C-015)
The calculator lead: the result creates a small profile with e-mail and name and a lead in the advisor's profile; the calculator runs under the advisor's path
The returning-customer page with the "what's new" section (section 3)
Web analytics (section 3), only with the visitor's consent, sent to the one tool that Provital names (A3-P-003)
A/B tests of the shop: a page or component variant, a visitor split and the result per variant. R1 runs one design
items.release: Readiness (pages and components can carry a variant): R1; the test function: R1.x

items.title: Virtual advisor stock is not in the platform. An advisor orders for a customer as any customer does, at the current conditions, and the ERP ships

Secondary functions by release. R1: re-order and the back-in-stock reminder. R1.x: the calculator lead (A3-C-024), the post library, the installable web app and push messages. Reviews, free samples, appointment booking and the charity add-on are not planned. R1.x: README section 4
No advisor voucher at R1. Head office steers the campaigns and vouchers centrally. The voucher function of the session notes is the ERP voucher article that the platform shows and redeems (A2-C-028)
A customer keeps several delivery addresses in the account. The ERP holds the invoice address
The redirect list with each source and target, including the pilot address (A7-D-003) with the advisor path as target; the cutover checks every entry
The product content per product, and the final brand book
The web analytics tool, cleared by the data protection officer
A journey starts on its trigger, sends at the set time, creates its task or stops on its condition
Every task shows its reason, its step list and its due date, and escalates after the deadline
A lead keeps its double opt-in and next step, and reaches the advisor whose link or path captured it
An approval case waits for customer service; another case runs into the ERP without a manual step. Every change on behalf of a customer sends the customer a message
For a complaint that starts in the platform, the feedback e-mail goes out after 72 hours only if no advisor message through the platform and no "done" on the task came first
The head office portal has the screens of the list confirmed in DP1 §3.3 and its admin functions. A role sees only what the staff-role rule set allows. Customer service reads statements only
No marketing or journey e-mail goes to a customer without a consent record that covers it. A transactional e-mail (order, password) needs no marketing consent
An advisor message shows the advisor's name as the sender, a reply reaches the advisor, and the customer profile logs the message
A registered advisor gets the advisor role only after the ERP records the approval, and an exit in the ERP ends the role
The journey engine: one trigger of a type of A4-O-001, channels (e-mail, task), timing, content, stop condition, escalation to a task

The journeys of Provital's journey rule set that use the trigger types of A4-O-001, set up by 57Blocks. Examples: first order, customer or pet birthday, anniversary, days since the last order, subscription end
The task list with the reason per item, the step list, the due date, the escalation after a deadline, and the handover to customer service
The 72-hour feedback rule (A4-O-005) for a complaint that starts in the platform (contact form, task, customer message)
The event catalogue: the platform events (order, delivery, account, consent, subscription, calculator, task) and the ERP events that an interface carries (invoice, payment, return)
The online lead: the form with a double opt-in, the lead in the advisor's profile with its next step, the consultation proposal, the reminders, and the expiry rule
The offline assisted lead: the advisor records the customer and sends a prepared basket by e-mail; the customer confirms and checks out
Advisor registration in the platform; approval and advisor number in the ERP; the role starts when the ERP records the approval
Offboarding: the ERP records the exit and the role ends. Head office moves customers and downline in the ERP, to the direct upline by default; the platform reads the result
The onboarding journey and its step list for a new advisor

The screens of the head office portal (DP1 §3.3): commission settings and the review of the monthly run; subscription cases; the clarification queue; the approval of a defined self-service case; the moderation of advisor content; the KPI and report screens for head office; the content function for …
items.release: RC: clarification queue, moderation, content function; others: R1

items.title: The self-service rule set: who may change what, which case needs an approval, the daily report of the changes to the customer-service lead
The e-mail function: templates per language, the send record, the bounce and complaint handling, and the unsubscribe per consent
The contact form to customer service: it creates a ticket through the open API and shows the ticket status in the customer account
The API to the e-mail marketing system: the event, segment and consent that campaigns need
The event and training entry in the advisor portal, with registration and reminder

Advisor e-mail: in the portal, the advisor writes or picks a prepared message for one of their customers. The platform sends it with the advisor's name as sender and the advisor's address as reply-to, checks the consent, and logs it in the customer profile. Not a mail link
Customer service reads an advisor's current and past statements (A1-C-016) in the commission screen, read only
Journey management for head office: create, edit, pause and end a journey, with a preview and a release step

The head office portal: a web application for Provital's staff, next to the shop and the advisor portal. Staff sign in through the company directory (T3-O-002). Each staff role sees only the screens and data that the staff-role rule set allows (T4-R-023). The audit log records each action …
The admin functions of the head office portal: the pilot switch per advisor (T3-C-001), data-subject requests (T3-C-003), and the staff roles with their assignment

R1 supports single-trigger journeys of three basic types: (1) a date (fixed date, birthday, anniversary); (2) a time relative to an event (days since the last order, days before the next delivery, days after registration); (3) an amount threshold (order value, points, spend in a period). R1 has no …

Customer service works per case: tickets in the ticket tool; subscription cases and approvals in the platform; returns in the ERP. Customer, advisor and customer service can each start a return or complaint request (A3-C-012)
Provital's current ticket tool, connected by its open API in both directions
E-mail and the task list are the channels at R1. WhatsApp and SMS are not in R1 and not in the R1.x list
No advisor message through the platform and no "done" on the task inside 72 hours counts as "not reachable" (A4-C-004)
The two lead processes in detail
The self-service workshop and its result
The e-mail texts per language and the sender identity
The access to the company directory for the head office portal, and the staff groups of the roles
An AI text stays inside the fixed page structure and the limit per advisor, and a person releases it before it is public
A text or a photo that matches a check rule produces a hint and a head-office entry, and waits for approval where the rule requires one
An upload produces a desktop and a mobile version at the minimum quality, and the original is kept
The crawler policy lists the open and the blocked paths. A test with an external crawler reaches no page behind a login and no customer or tracking data on the listed paths
Each AI function can be switched off on its own, and the record shows the call, the function and the cost
The chatbot test set contains cases that try to obtain another customer's data. The function meets its pass level on them. A handover reaches the advisor or the contact form (R1.x)
The export for Provital's own AI contains only released data with a consent base, and no personal data of a customer
An accepted regional match creates a lead for the matched advisor and changes no assignment of a customer to an advisor (R1.x)
A text in the content function that matches the health-claim list shows a hint, and a person can still release it
Each advertisement parameter of the rule set opens its section with the matching animals and products
Each AI translation waits for a person's release, and a person can override it (R1.x)
An advisor publishes only an approved post of the library to a connected channel (R1.x)
The advisor text help: a generated draft from the advisor's data and their keywords, inside the fixed structure of the page and the limits per advisor
The text check finds an unlawful claim, a missing imprint or a prohibited comparison. It shows a hint to the advisor and creates a moderation entry for head office
The photo check finds a photo with a low resolution, recognisable persons, an external logo or a before-and-after claim
The health-claim hint in the content function (A5-C-015), as an internal hint for Provital
Personalisation at entry: the advertisement parameter decides the section, the animals and the products
The AI gateway: one connection to the model provider, with the prompt per function, the record of each call, the cost limit and the off switch per function
The AI-readable site and the crawler policy: public pages readable by an external agent, deeper access blocked
The customer chatbot: it guides to a product or to the advisor, with the advisor's reachable hours and channels
The internal chatbot for an advisor: business and service questions, and a handover to the contact form, an e-mail or the ticket tool
Order help: order status, tracking and the return request after a login, with an identity check on the general site
Recommendations after a login, from the customer's animals and their last orders

AI translation into the languages that the platform runs (R1: German and English), with a human override. A further language follows after R1 through change control (T3-D-014); DR lists the difference
The social media post library: an advisor publishes an approved picture, video or text to a connected channel (Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest, TikTok)
The advisory agent on a content base, with the content owner and the source list

The content function: a draft and a released version, a language per market and a preview, for these page types: a general landing page, a product-focused page, category pages, product pages, content pages with text, image and video blocks, and a page with frequent questions
The media pipeline: one upload produces a desktop and a mobile version at a minimum quality; the platform stores the variants and the original
The advisor's social links and contact data on the page, each item set public or private
The data export for Provital's own AI: the released, anonymous data set with its consent base, in a documented format
Purchase help on Provital's own site, when the visitor wants no advisor
The regional advisor match: a guiding question offers a matching advisor in the visitor's region; an accepted match creates a lead for that advisor (A4)
The AI release split of section 4
The legal basis of each AI function

All AI functions use the gateway. The processing agreement forbids training on platform data. The provider runs in the European Union or at a location that Provital approves. Provital approves the provider before its first use
The advisory content at R1 is the calculator logic and Provital's product and care texts. The advisory agent follows in R1.x
After a violation, customer service approves each photo of that advisor before it goes live; text changes of that advisor also wait for approval. Both end when the check rules release the advisor
Assumption: legal counsel confirms that anonymous customer and advisor data may serve Provital's own AI
The owner of the chatbot answers and the chatbot rule set (section 5)
A change of a token changes every screen that uses it, without a code change
Each screen of the inventory exists in the mobile and the desktop layout, at the defined breakpoints
The accessibility test of A6-O-003 runs on the areas of the target, shows no open item of level A, and its report lists each other open item with a plan
The handover file documents the tokens, the components and the rules, so that a later agency can design a component in the same style
The final colours, typeface and logo are applied through the tokens, without a change to any screen layout
The design tokens on the relaunch branding: colour, type, spacing, radius, shadow, the logo and the claim, with a light and a high-contrast variant
The component library: navigation, product card, price and points, add to cart, form fields, validation messages, modal, table, the account navigation, the portal widgets

The screen inventory: the entry pages, the category and product page, the cart, the checkout, the confirmation, the account, the subscription, the return, the advisor page, the portal dashboard, the to-do list, the figures and the screens of the head office portal
The responsive rules: the mobile breakpoints, the touch targets, the table behaviour on a small screen, the image formats per breakpoint
The accessibility baseline: contrast, focus, labels, keyboard order, the statement page
The design handover: the documented tokens, the components and the rules, and the review file per screen
The shell of the installable web app (PWA) and the design of push notifications
The design system starts on the work-in-progress brand book. The final values replace the tokens
One approver, named by Provital, and one review each week

The accessibility target is WCAG 2.2 AA for the shop, the account, the checkout and the advisor portal, with a statement page and a named contact. Test: an automated check on every screen of these areas and a manual test of the key flows. The test report lists each open item with a plan. Head …
Two or three reference websites per area
Each pilot order reaches NAV once, with the right advisor and the right payment, or waits in the clarification queue with its reason
The cutover runs inside the window; every runbook step has an owner and a result
The activity log of the rehearsal lists every order, account, consent and subscription change and exports in a documented format

Page variants. The shop pages are built so that page variants can run later. The A/B test function itself is R1.x

A modular monolith, deployed as one application with one worker process (built from the same code base), with clear module boundaries: commerce, subscription, commission, journey, content, identity, integration

Background work runs in a worker, not in the request: the due-delivery run, the commission run, the journey triggers, the outbox, the copies and the reconciliation
One PostgreSQL database, one object store for media, one queue. No second database for a module
Every module reaches the ERP only through the integration module and its port (one fixed set of operations towards the ERP). The NAV adapter and the Business Central adapter each implement that port

The platform is provider-neutral: it runs on a container platform on any of the three major clouds. The application uses no managed service that only one cloud provider offers (database, queue, object store and container runtime follow open standards). The external services of T2 section 4.3 are …

The front end is server-rendered for the shop and the advisor page, and client-rendered for the advisor portal and the head office portal (A4-C-020)
